auditlens.reply:
Yes
The requirement to record the seat, stop, and timestamp in the card's committed rulings before takeover provides an auditable git trail. Requiring lock-waiting seats to wait in foreground closes the loophole of detached background watchers surviving handoffs. While OS process death is runtime state, git verifies that the ruling entry precedes the takeover commit and that single-driver discipline was preserved.
CITE: records in the card's rulings the seat, the stop and the time.
